From 29 June to 3 July, Technological University Dublin (TU Dublin) hosted EUt+ Week, bringing together academics, researchers, students and institutional leaders from across the European University of Technology alliance (EUt+).

external_collaboration.partner_name: Università degli Studi di Cassino e del Lazio Meridionale
external_collaboration.evidence_quote: Looking ahead EUt+ Week at TU Dublin provided an opportunity to strengthen existing partnerships, develop new collaborations and advance important work across research, education, student engagement and institutional development. The momentum generated during the week will continue as members of the alliance prepare for the next EUt+ physical meeting, which will take place in September at Università degli Studi di Cassino e del Lazio Meridionale in Italy.

Coming together to sing and gain intercultural experience: that was the approach of a project week organised at Darmstadt University of Applied Sciences (h_da) for staff of the European partner universities in the EUT+ alliance. What fun it is to sing songs together without understanding the language! Another insight was that singing connects and motivates people – something that can also be put to professional use.

The participants, who communicate with each other in English, observe the same effect. “My very first encounter with the English language was via music,” recalls Rosella Tinaburri from the Language Centre at the University of Cassino, Italy. At the time, she really liked the U2 song “I Still Haven’t Found What I’m Looking For”, which inspired her to learn the language.
